correctness.rationale: Newton identities valid for p>=5 identify first 3 power sums with elementary-symmetric regular sequence. A rank-deficient 3x n Jacobian is equivalent by Vandermonde to <=2 coordinate values; first two sum equations and 0<a,b<n<2p force exactly p copies of a nonzero value and r zeroes projectively. On an affine chart at each such point, the first two independent gradients eliminate U,V and the remaining quadratic form is nondegenerate: its two I+J blocks have determinants p-1 (nonzero mod p) and r (nonzero mod p). Formal Morse lemma in odd characteristic gives ordinary double point and reduced Jacobian singular scheme. S2 complete intersection plus finite codim>=2 singular support yields R1/normality; projective CI connectedness plus normality gives integrality. In the smallest (p,r)=(5,1), independent exhaustive P^5(F5) singular census finds six, and Hessian determinants check examples, not the general geometric proof.
